display.title: Episode 201: Yosef Mokir Shabbos
display.summary_short: Entries pour in for the 'My Mezuzah' contest, a class leads the Shema, a phone quiz on how a mezuzah is made, and the story of Yosef who honored Shabbos.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi reports a pile of beautiful entries in the 'My Mezuzah' contest and describes one in detail, a six-year-old's purple cloth mezuzah with a golden border, a sewn-on letter of Hashem's Name and lace. Everyone who beautifies a mitzvah is a winner, he says, and the contest runs until Chanukah. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, a second-grade class from Beis Yaakov of Borough Park visits Studio 604 and leads the Shema. Mitzvah Time's phone quiz goes to a fifth-grader who correctly explains that a mezuzah is written on parchment from a kosher animal, with a quill from a kosher bird and black ink. Story time tells of Yosef Mokir Shabbos, who every Thursday carried home the biggest fish in the market and shared gefilte fish with the town's poor in honor of Shabbos, while his rich neighbor never gave a penny. A stargazer warns the rich man that his wealth will pass to Yosef, so he turns everything into one diamond sewn into his hat, which the wind blows into the sea. One Friday fishermen sell Yosef a giant fish, and inside it is the diamond. As the Sages say, whoever spends for Shabbos, Shabbos repays.
display.lesson: Whatever you spend in honor of Shabbos, Hashem repays in full; and sharing with others brings blessing.

date.note: Six weeks after 195 (Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan, 1985-10-15) and ten before 211 (1986-02-04); contest 'until Chanukah'. No date said on air.

privacy.note: A six-year-old contest entrant and a phone-quiz winner are named in full.
